events.title: One Pair Across Every Shot
must_haves: One assembled 15-second 16:9 film tells the story in three distinct shots.
The woman retains the same facial structure, freckles and red pixie cut in all three shots.
The man retains the same facial structure, shaved head and round glasses in all three shots; the two identities never merge or swap.
Both faces are clearly visible in every shot, not hidden by rear views, distant framing or object-only cutaways.
The red scarf is dropped by the woman, picked up by the man and returned to her in that order, ending with mutual smiles.
The film looks realistic and has no audible soundtrack.

answer_sheet.Character identities: An adult woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut, and an adult man with a shaved head and round glasses. Invent their faces but keep each identity unchanged across all three shots.
answer_sheet.Face visibility: Both faces must be clearly visible in every shot, including when the scarf is dropped and picked up.
answer_sheet.Story and setting: On a quiet street, the woman drops a red scarf, the man picks it up, and he returns it before they smile at each other.
answer_sheet.Length and format: One 15-second widescreen 16:9 video in three shots.
answer_sheet.Style and mood: Realistic live action, a small friendly encounter.
answer_sheet.Sound and text: Silent, with no captions, titles or dialogue.

events.text: Could you make a realistic, silent story in three shots about a small encounter on a quiet street, with both people being adults? I like these little moments of kindness because they remind me of how much a brief interaction can mean. The woman has a freckled face and a red pixie cut, and she drops a red scarf in the first shot. The whole thing should be a 15-second widescreen video, and in the second shot a man with a shaved head and round glasses picks the scarf up. In the third shot, he returns it to her and they smile. My main worry is that the people might look like different actors after a cut. Please show both faces clearly in every shot and keep exactly the same two faces throughout, with no changing actors between cuts.

events.text: I’ll stage three five-second shots, keeping both adults’ faces visible and repeating their identifying details across each cut. {"name":"A Small Kindness — Three-Shot Silent Story","end_seconds":15,"aspect_ratio":"16:9","model":"default","audio":false,"style":{"prompt":"Create a realistic live-action silent short film, exactly 15 seconds, widescreen 16:9. Exactly THREE shots, hard cuts at 5 seconds and 10 seconds. A tiny warm moment of kindness on a quiet residential street in soft overcast daylight. Exactly two people, BOTH clearly ADULTS around 35 years old. No other people, no text, no dialogue, no music, no audio.
CRITICAL CAST CONTINUITY: Use exactly the SAME TWO ACTORS with exactly the SAME TWO FACES in all three shots. Lock facial geometry, eye color, skin tone, hair, glasses, clothing and age across cuts. Never recast, morph, beautify or replace either person. Woman: adult, oval fair freckled face, freckles clearly across cheeks and nose, green eyes, short RED PIXIE haircut, navy wool coat, charcoal trousers. Man: adult, medium-brown skin, shaved BALD head, distinctive ROUND thin black glasses, brown eyes, clean-shaven oval face, olive jacket, beige trousers. One bright RED SCARF, identical scarf throughout. Both are strangers, gentle natural expressions. Preserve the same quiet street, daylight and screen direction across cuts.
Every shot is a frontal or gentle three-quarter TWO-SHOT with BOTH faces clearly visible, recognizable, unobstructed and in focus. Moderate depth of field, eye-level camera, no rear views, no face close-ups that exclude the other actor, no face-obscuring hands. Frame both adults from knees up with the ground/scarf visible as needed. They stand close enough together for both faces to be readable. Simple natural performance, no exaggerated movements.
SHOT 1, 0-5 seconds: Establish both adults walking slowly near one another on an empty pavement, woman screen left and man screen right. Both faces are clearly seen. The red scarf slips from the woman's hand and falls onto the pavement between them. She pauses, unaware, looking slightly ahead; he notices the dropped scarf. Keep both faces visible throughout.
HARD CUT at 5 seconds.
SHOT 2, 5-10 seconds: Same street and EXACT SAME two actors, same faces and wardrobe. Frontal medium-wide two-shot. The man, still screen right, bends at the knees, his face angled up in three-quarter view and round glasses visible, and picks up the red scarf with one hand. The woman stands screen left, her freckled face and red pixie cut clearly visible, and turns slightly toward him. Both faces remain in frame, unobstructed and recognizable during the pickup. He rises holding the scarf.
HARD CUT at 10 seconds.
SHOT 3, 10-15 seconds: Frontal medium two-shot of EXACT SAME actors. Man screen right offers the same red scarf to woman screen left; she takes it. Both faces clearly visible in gentle three-quarter view toward camera as they exchange small sincere grateful smiles and brief eye contact. Hold the shared smile to the end. Understated documentary realism, believable hands and scarf physics, stable anatomy, natural skin texture, consistent faces through every cut. No additional cuts, no montage, no transitions or fade."}}
